title: Mousafiris
body:
There was a flower:
my grandmother called it "mousafiris"—
that is, a guest.
Because, with a gentle breeze, it scattered
—it had fragile bonds—
and sought hospitality
wherever the wind carried it.
On my grandfather's hoe,
in my grandmother's dustpan,
in the puddle of the newly watered apricot tree;
dismembered, yet coexisting with intact nature.

To my grandmother, all people
were mousafirides.

y.f.
